review_evidence: README describes a Lean 4 bitmap/PNG library with verified encode/decode support and proofs of functional correctness, termination, buffer safety, and format invariants.

The large Bitmap/Lemmas/Png subtree consists of fine-grained correctness lemmas for DEFLATE, filtering, chunks, palette handling, Adam7, and round trips; these are the mathematical/proof content of the project rather than generated reports.
Bitmap/Tests.lean and other test-named modules are formal Lean sources within the proof-bearing library, and FILTER-011 gives no basis for path-only removal; no safe hard exclusion was established.
summary: Retain the entire Bitmap Lean proof corpus; implementation, lemma, and test modules all contribute verified PNG/bitmap behavior.

review_evidence: Bitmap/Lemmas/Png/EncodeDecodeBaseU32.lean (smallest, 7318 bytes): 5 lemmas, e.g. u32be_size and readU32BE_u32be (big-endian 32-bit round trip) with full tactic proofs.
Bitmap/Lemmas/Png/Lz77Dynamic.lean (largest): 129 declarations, 112 lemmas, e.g. defs dynamicPayloadLz77TokenBitLen/StreamBits and lemma writeDynamicPayloadLz77Token_literal_eq_writeBits.
Bitmap/Png.lean: 559 declarations of the PNG implementation (u16le, u32be, readU32BE, crc32Table, crc32Update, ...) that the lemma modules state properties of.

Bitmap/Lemmas/Png/DynamicBlockProofsPayloadFixedDecodeLen8.lean and Len9.lean: each holds one long lemma (fixedLitLenHuffman_decode_readerAt_writeBits_len8_core / len9_core) that spans the whole file.
Bitmap/Lemmas/Png/FixedBlockFastSlowBridge.lean: 20 lemmas on BitReader, e.g. readBit_lt_two and readBitsAux_lt_two_pow.
Bitmap/Lemmas/Png/DynamicBlockProofsReadTablesConcrete.lean: lemma readDynamicTables_readerAt_writeBits_concrete plus a private helper lemma.
Other listed files have these lemma counts: Basic 127, CoreByteArray 23, DynamicBlockProofsPayloadTail 20, DynamicEncoderDecode 84, FixedBlockProofsDecode 34, FixedBlockProofsSpec 8, Lz77 31.
summary: Declaration-keyword counts over all 15 files plus direct reads of the smallest file and the heads of the largest files show that every file holds Lean definitions, lemmas, and proofs about PNG, zlib, DEFLATE, LZ77, and bit-level encode/decode correctness. No file is a data table, import aggregator, or build script, so every file stays searchable.
